title: Production incident triage trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for endpoint-broken-in-prod trace events: one production incident being triaged — the worksheet (phases, facts, signals, suspects) plus the stopwatch.

service.description: The service the incident is about, e.g. employee-api.

endpoint.description: The endpoint named in the report, e.g. 'GET /employees'.

report.description: The report as it was received, verbatim and unverified.

stage.description: Technical lifecycle state of the incident, translated by the visualizer.

severity.description: Derived from the measured blast radius, never asserted; 'unknown' until the radius is measured.

minutes.description: Minutes charged since the report landed; every action has a fixed deterministic cost.

phases.description: The eight triage phases, always in order: clarify, reproduce, measure, mitigate, diagnose, fix, verify, prevent.

name.description: Technical phase code, translated by the visualizer.

state.description: 'skipped' means a later phase was reached while this one was never touched.

detail.description: What was done in this phase, e.g. the mitigation action or the fix.

facts.description: The questions asked of the reporter, in order, with the answer when there is one.

question.description: The question put to whoever reported the incident.

answer.description: The answer, or null while the question is still open.

known.description: Whether this question has an answer yet.

reproduction.description: The attempt to send the failing request yourself; absent until one is made.

request.description: The request as it was sent, including whose parameters and token it used.

failed.description: Whether it reproduced the failure; false narrows the search rather than closing it.

observed.description: What actually came back, e.g. '500 employee.internal_error'.

signals.description: Metrics and logs read during triage, in the order they were read.

name.description: What was read, e.g. '5xx rate on GET /employees'.

value.description: The reading itself, or '-' when the signal does not exist.

verdict.description: 'missing' is a finding about observability, not about the bug.

blastRadius.description: The measured scope of the incident; absent until it is measured.

affected.description: What is affected, e.g. 'GET /employees for 6 of 41 departments'.

share.description: Percentage of traffic affected; the severity is derived from this number.

clients.description: Which callers are hit, e.g. 'the HR web client and the payroll sync job'.

mitigation.description: What restored service; absent while nothing has been mitigated.

action.description: The reversible action taken, e.g. 'roll back to the previous release'.

effect.description: What it did to the signals, e.g. '5xx rate back to 0.1%'.

suspects.description: The hypotheses about what is different, in the order they were raised.

name.description: The suspected difference, e.g. 'the nightly HR import'.

why.description: Why it is on the list at all.

status.description: Where the hypothesis stands; it never leaves 'open' without evidence.

evidence.description: What closed it, in either direction; empty while it is still open.

rootCause.description: The confirmed cause, or null while nothing is confirmed.

testGap.description: Why the test suite was green, or null while nobody has answered that.

fixApplied.description: The change shipped against the cause, or null while nothing has been changed.

verified.description: Whether re-running the failing request succeeded; null while nothing has been verified.

guards.description: Follow-ups that would make the next incident of this class shorter.

missteps.description: Triage errors recorded as consequences of the order actions were taken in.

openQuestions.description: How many asked questions still have no answer.
